method.instrument: probe.js, evaluated in a headed browser pane against the vendored Origami Simulator at web/frontend/dist/simulator/index.html?embed=1
method.no_self_collision: thickenModel/thickenOffset are RENDERING options; this solver has no self-intersection handling, so layers pass through each other and residual thickness is NOT paper thickness
method.planarity_definition: smallest/largest principal standard deviation of the folded vertex cloud (symmetric 3x3 eigensolve of its covariance). A flat-folded sheet is a PLANE, so this goes to ~0.
method.protocol_replicated: mcp_harness/sim_capture.py SimSession.capture: loadFold -> setFold(percent) -> settle -> getFoldedGeometry
method.renderer: WebGL 1.0, ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4)
method.validation: the anchor reproduced sim_capture.ANCHOR_DISP = 1.3109 EXACTLY, which is what licenses the other readings
method.why_not_playwright: playwright is not installed in this venv and no browser cache exists; the protocol was replicated in a headed browser pane instead

runs.drive: RAMP 10->100 in steps of 10, 4 s each
runs.subject: dense lizard (SAT witness)

seeding_attempt.injected_not_committed: run by evaluating the logic in-page; no file in this branch was modified
seeding_attempt.mechanism: writes targetTheta * creasePercent into the solver's u_theta and u_lastTheta textures after the model syncs, so creases start on the branch of their target rather than at 0 where the sign is decided by sub-precision noise
seeding_attempt.note_on_745: exactly the fold's crease count; the other 364 are triangulation diagonals with targetTheta 0
seeding_attempt.prior_art: seedTheta, taken VERBATIM from .claude/worktrees/origami-animal-models-a131b6/web/frontend/public/simulator/js/ide-bridge.js (not merged to this branch; the shipped dist bridge has only loadFold/setFold/getFoldedGeometry)
seeding_attempt.question: does seeding each crease's unwrapped angle AT its target, instead of letting all 745 start at zero, let the solver reach the flat state?
seeding_attempt.structural_finding: seeding crease ANGLE BRANCHES is not seeding the LAYER ORDER. This solver has no self-collision, so layer order has no physical effect in it and no degree of freedom represents it. The SAT result is not consumable by this simulator at all -- not for want of effort, but because the state it constrains does not exist in this model.
seeding_attempt.verdict: NO EFFECT ON THE ATTRACTOR. Seeded converges to ~0.063-0.064 against unseeded 0.06482 -- a different trajectory to the same destination. The non-flatness is NOT the solver starting creases on the wrong angular branch.

METHODOLOGICAL_FAILURE.cause: the sweep helper called loadFold but never reloaded the page, so each run started from the previous config's relaxed positions. It measured config PLUS history, not config.
METHODOLOGICAL_FAILURE.clean_retest: 0.08354, i.e. WORSE than the 0.06591 baseline, inverting the sign of the original claim
METHODOLOGICAL_FAILURE.detection: re-running faceStiffness 1.0 after a different predecessor gave 0.05556 instead of 0.03559 -- same config, different answer
METHODOLOGICAL_FAILURE.what: a first sweep reported faceStiffness 1.0 at planarity 0.03559, a 45% improvement over baseline. It was WRONG.
METHODOLOGICAL_FAILURE.why_it_looked_sound: this solver is DETERMINISTIC (its tie-break jitter is a Knuth hash, not random), so re-running an identical sequence reproduced bit-identical numbers. Stability was mistaken for validity.

solver_parameter_sweep.answer: NO. Raising it makes the result WORSE.
solver_parameter_sweep.clean_method: full page reload per run; config set before loadFold; 30-60 s settle
solver_parameter_sweep.question: the solver's faceStiffness defaults to 0.2, which is soft for paper (paper facets do not stretch). Does raising it let the relaxation reach flat?
solver_parameter_sweep.verdict: three independent levers, none moves the attractor. The dense CP settles at planarity ~0.065 against sparse 0.00586 and the anchor 0.00002.
